questions.question: Evaluate the role of invertebrate fossils in paleogeographic reconstructions. Also / discuss how fossil assemblages help in identifying past continental positions and marine connections.
questions.solution_html:
• Invertebrate fossils in paleogeographic reconstructions.
  • • Continental Positions: Using fossil distributions (e.g., Glossopteris or specific trilobites) to
  • prove former land connections (Gondwana).
  • • Marine Connections: Identifying shared marine fauna between now-separated basins to
  • indicate ancient seaways or barriers.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain conditions of fossilization. Add a note on body fossils.
questions.solution_html:
• • Conditions: 1. Preservation of original soft part without alteration. 2. Preservation of original
  • hard part without alteration. 3. Preservation of altered hard parts. 4. Preservation of traces
  • or evidence of animal activities.
  • • Body Fossils: Remains of the actual organism (shells, bones, teeth) preserved via
  • permineralization, replacement, or moulds/casts.

questions.question: Describe the internal parts of a Cephalopod shell, focusing on siphuncle, septa, / septal necks, connecting rings and chambers.
questions.solution_html:
• Internal parts of a Cephalopod shell.
  • • Septa & Chambers: Cross-walls (septa) that divide the shell into gas-filled buoyancy
  • chambers (camerae).
  • • Siphuncle: A tube of living tissue extending through the septa to regulate buoyancy.
  • Marks]
  • • Septal Necks: Extensions of the septa that support the siphuncle at the point of entry.
  • Marks]
  • • Connecting Rings: Segments of the siphuncle between the septal necks.
questions.final_answer: • Connecting Rings: Segments of the siphuncle between the septal necks
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain Palaeontology definition, scope and applications.
questions.solution_html:
• Palaeontology: Definition, scope, and applications.
  • • Definition: The study of ancient life through fossils.
  • • Scope: Includes Palaeobotany, Palaeozoology, Micropalaeontology, and Ichnology.
  • • Applications
  • o Geological: Age determination, correlation, and stratigraphy.
  • o Biological/Industrial: Understanding evolution, paleoclimate studies, and
  • exploration for fossil fuels /Oil).
